module_title: Arbitration Agreement, Kompetenz-Kompetenz, and Interim Reliefs
introduction: This intermediate tier dissects the mechanics of initiating an arbitration. It covers the doctrine of severability, the absolute power of the tribunal to decide its own jurisdiction, and the parallel powers of the Court and the Tribunal to grant emergency reliefs.

core_concepts.title: The Arbitration Agreement (Section 7)
core_concepts.description:
The foundation of the entire process.
- Definition: An agreement by the parties to submit to arbitration all or certain disputes which have arisen or may arise between them in respect of a defined legal relationship, whether contractual or not.
- Doctrine of Severability (Section 16(1)): If a main contract is declared null and void, the arbitration clause embedded inside it survives as an independent agreement. The death of the contract does not kill the arbitration clause.

core_concepts.title: Power to Refer Parties to Arbitration (Section 8)
core_concepts.description:
If parties have an arbitration agreement but one party mischievously files a civil suit in a regular court, the other party can apply to the court under Section 8. 
- The Rule: The judicial authority MUST refer the parties to arbitration if a valid agreement exists. The application must be made not later than the date of submitting the first statement on the substance of the dispute (the Written Statement).

core_concepts.title: Kompetenz-Kompetenz (Section 16)
core_concepts.description:
A fundamental doctrine meaning 'Competence-Competence'.
- The Rule: The Arbitral Tribunal has the supreme authority to rule on its own jurisdiction, including ruling on any objections with respect to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement. The courts cannot prematurely interfere to stop an arbitration claiming the tribunal lacks jurisdiction.

core_concepts.title: Interim Measures: Court vs. Tribunal (Section 9 vs. Section 17)
core_concepts.description:
Parties often need emergency orders (e.g., freezing bank accounts, preserving goods) before the final award.
- Section 9 (By the Court): A party can apply to the civil court for interim relief *before* the arbitral proceedings begin, during the proceedings, or even after the award is passed (but before enforcement).
- Section 17 (By the Tribunal): Once the Arbitral Tribunal is constituted, parties MUST seek interim relief from the Tribunal under Section 17, not the court. Post-2015 amendment, an interim order passed by the Tribunal under Sec 17 has the exact same enforceability as an order of a civil court.

important_entities.name: Appointment of Arbitrators (Section 11)
important_entities.key_fact: Courts step in when party machinery fails.
important_entities.significance: Parties are free to agree on a procedure for appointing the arbitrator(s). If they fail to agree within 30 days, or if two appointed arbitrators fail to agree on the third presiding arbitrator, a party can apply to the High Court (for domestic) or the Supreme Court (for international commercial arbitration) to make the appointment.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Can parties agree to appoint exactly 2 or 4 arbitrators? **NO**. Under Section 10, the parties are free to determine the number of arbitrators, provided that such number shall **not be an even number**. This guarantees a majority decision can be reached to avoid deadlocks. If the agreement fails to specify, the default consists of a sole arbitrator.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 9 is the Judge, 17 is the Arbitrator.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Section 9 dictates court-ordered interim relief; Section 17 dictates tribunal-ordered interim relief.

exam_strategy_tips: If an exam asks 'Which legal doctrine allows an arbitration clause to survive even if the main contract is declared void?', select the **Doctrine of Severability (or Separability)**.
